dimensions.title: Cognitive
milestones: Begins to understand cause and effect
Can solve simple problems, like pulling a toy out of a container
Recognizes familiar objects and people
activities: Engage in simple shape sorting toys
watchFor: Limited ability to explore new toys

dimensions.title: Language
milestones: Can say a few words like 'mama' or 'dada'
Understands simple commands
Responds to their name

dimensions.title: Physical
milestones: Starts to stand without support
Can walk while holding onto furniture
Picks up small objects with thumb and finger
activities: Provide push toys for walking support
Create a safe space for crawling and climbing
Encourage throwing and kicking soft balls
watchFor: Not attempting to stand or walk
Lack of interest in physical activity

dimensions.title: Social
milestones: Shows interest in being around other children
Begins to express emotions like joy and frustration
Imitates simple actions of adults and older children
activities: Encourage shared activities like building blocks
watchFor: Difficulty engaging in play with peers

dimensions.title: Emotional
milestones: Expresses a range of emotions including happiness, anger, and sadness
Begins to show attachment to familiar caregivers
Can be comforted by familiar individuals
activities: Introduce soft toys for emotional expression

dimensions.title: Curiosity
milestones: Explores the environment by crawling or walking
Shows interest in how things work
Investigates objects by banging, shaking, or mouthing
activities: Set up a safe exploration area
Provide various textures and materials to explore
Encourage outdoor play and nature exploration
watchFor: Limited exploration or play with new objects
Fear or avoidance of new experiences

dimensions.title: Learning
milestones: Can focus on a task for a short period
Begins to understand simple concepts like 'in' and 'out'
Shows persistent attempts to reach a goal
activities: Engage in short, focused play sessions
watchFor: Quick loss of interest in play

dimensions.title: Independence
milestones: Can begin self-feeding with finger foods
Shows preference for certain toys or activities
Mimics adult behaviors like brushing hair
activities: Include child in daily routines like getting dressed
watchFor: Excessive dependence on caregivers for tasks
